source.title: City of Lowell FY2025 Adopted Budget

meta.note: Lowell reports its budget on three official bases; this tree uses the all-funds total (583,735,930), the one whose categories add up exactly. The General Fund operating budget is $473.8M; water/sewer/parking are self-supporting enterprise funds; the City Council voted a $519.9M appropriation. FY2025 is Lowell's most recent ADOPTED budget (FY2026 is still only proposed).
facts: Schools are about 49% of the budget — Lowell Public Schools = $257.1M, most of it state Chapter 70 aid.
State "cherry sheet" assessments hit $49.7M, up from $29.2M in FY2020 — driven mainly by charter-school tuition, the city's biggest fiscal pressure.
Lowell is the 5th-largest city in Massachusetts, a designated Gateway City, and taxes business property at nearly double the residential rate.

departments.name: Education (Lowell Public Schools)
departments.what: Schools — about half the whole budget. Most of it is state Chapter 70 aid.

departments.name: General Government
departments.what: Pensions, health insurance, and state/county assessments the city must pay.

departments.what: Streets, water, sewer, trash, and city facilities.

departments.name: Debt Service (capital)
departments.what: Paying off money borrowed for buildings — including the new Lowell High School.

departments.what: Health, the Council on Aging, veterans, and recreation.
